page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c2.xlarge is a virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is provisioned with 16 dedicated virtual CPUs based on the x86_64 architecture and provides 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not feature onboard GPU acceleration, operating with zero GPUs.

Storage configuration for the ecs.c2.xlarge does not include bundled local disks, meaning persistent storage must be provisioned via external network-attached volumes. Similarly, the instance is allocated zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses upon creation, requiring external network configuration or elastic IP binding for public routing. Benchmark metrics across standard CPU, memory bandwidth, compression, and inference evaluations are not provided in the specification profile.

From an infrastructure and cost efficiency perspective, dedicating 16 physical-to-virtual cores with 64.0 GB of RAM places this configuration into a general-purpose operational envelope. Because storage is separated from compute, resource costs can be managed independently from data persistence. Tradeoffs include the dependency on remote storage bandwidth for I/O performance and the lack of hardware vector acceleration flags such as AVX-512.

The ecs.c2.xlarge instance profile is aligned with multi-threaded application tiers that demand steady compute allocation without excessive memory footprints. Suitable deployment targets include enterprise application servers, mid-sized relational database environments, container host clusters, CI/CD runners, and general web serving workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c2.xlarge is a dedicated virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs alongside 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual processor. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external block storage for data persistence, nor does it include built-in GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With full compute dedication and an uncoupled storage model, resource allocation remains predictable while operational expenditure is tied strictly to provisioned infrastructure. The balanced memory-to-core balance positions this server for balanced business workloads, including web application clusters, continuous integration workers, enterprise middleware, and standard backend database services.
